name: Murree Road Metrobus viaduct and typical elevated station
assumptions: No photograph of Committee Chowk station itself was found: the station design is taken from photos of 6th Road station, assuming the elevated stations share one design, as the matching photo captions and repair reports suggest.
Which end of the Committee Chowk roof is high is unknown: the high end and entrance canopy are placed at the north.
Road deck 9.5 m above the origin, fitted to vehicles and riders beside the piers; no published deck height.
Road level is held flat; the real deck rises and falls over the Murree Road underpass and terrain.
Pier spacing 26 m from the audit girder length; pier phase along the road is arbitrary and the same in the split section.
Deck section (two trapezoid boxes, a third under the island, cantilevers) is read from soffit photos; the audit also lists I and inverted-T girders.
Width at the station: OSM leg spacing 12 m plus a lane and parapet each side, about 17.6 m in all; the single deck is 9.2 m (audit).
Roof profile: hump 6.6 m, valley 3.8 m and peak 8.0 m above the road at the side walls, and their positions along the 117.8 m length, are fitted to one telephoto photo with a perspective correction.
Six pergola portals counted from three photos; pergola top 7.3 m above the road.

Concourse block in the median, its 3.0 to 4.5 m slab, the truss and the escalator housing follow 6th Road photos; layout at Committee Chowk and access bridges are unknown, and the steel pedestrian bridges are left out.
Platform screen doors are not modelled: Wikipedia confirms they exist but no source or photo shows their layout.
All colours are estimates from photos. Night glow of glass and street lamps is a guess; no source describes station lighting.
Model covers about 352 m centred on the station; the rest of the corridor is outside this landmark.
